questions.stem: In a patient with loose teeth, which two airway devices should be avoided?
questions.answer: Oropharyngeal airway (OPA) and laryngeal mask airway (LMA)

questions.stem: What is the medicolegal significance of dental injury under general anaesthesia?
options: It is rarely reported to medicolegal bodies
It is the most common cause of complaints and claims against anaesthetists
It is mainly a problem of regional anaesthesia
It causes most cases of postoperative nausea

questions.stem: What is the estimated incidence of dental injury under general anaesthesia?
options: 1% to 5% of GAs
0.02% to 0.1% of GAs
0.5% to 1% of GAs
10% to 20% of GAs

questions.stem: In dental injury risk, which age group has mixed dentition?
options: Infants under 12 months
Adults over 30 years old
Children aged 5-12 years old
Children aged 13-18 years old

questions.stem: What decides whether an avulsed permanent tooth survives?
What is the treatment of choice for an avulsed permanent tooth?
options: Replant within 30 minutes
Dry storage and a clinic visit later
Replant within 5 minutes, pressing it into the socket
Discard it and arrange a dental implant

questions.stem: If an avulsed permanent tooth cannot be replanted within 5 minutes, how should it be kept?
options: Dry, wrapped in gauze
Dry, in a sealed container
In a storage medium such as saline or cold fresh milk, never dry
In tap water at room temperature

questions.stem: What should be done with fragments from a crown fracture or broken prosthesis?
questions.answer: Keep them in a storage medium and give them to the patient for urgent dental review

questions.stem: How is bleeding from the socket of an avulsed tooth controlled?
After a dental injury under general anaesthesia, which specialist review is needed immediately?
What is the treatment of an avulsed primary (milk) tooth?
options: Replant it immediately
Store it in saline and replant it later
Refer for an urgent implant
No treatment needed

questions.stem: Why should an avulsed primary (milk) tooth not be replanted?
options: It will not survive if replanted
It can cause bleeding into the airway
It can damage the permanent tooth erupting beneath
It always causes pulp necrosis in the child

questions.stem: What should a patient with loose teeth be counselled about before anaesthesia?
How can mobile teeth be secured during anaesthesia to stop them falling into the airway?
Which airway adjunct should be avoided in a patient with loose teeth because it can dislodge them?
options: Video laryngoscope blade
Oropharyngeal airway
Gum elastic bougie
Intubating stylet

questions.stem: Compared with direct laryngoscopy, what does video laryngoscopy offer a patient with loose teeth?
options: Greater force needed to lift the jaw
Uses the upper teeth more as a fulcrum
Less forceful lifting and less upper-teeth fulcrum
Eliminates any risk of dislodging a tooth
